docs.purpose: Gives the admin dashboard a fast, lightweight snapshot of each pipeline's latest run status, meant to be polled frequently without the overhead of the full stats endpoint's thirty-plus counting queries.
docs.data_story: It reads 1 table — `pipeline_runs` and writes nothing. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 8 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 1 place: `admin_data_quality`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: No SPEC LINK or spec citation in the file. No verifyAdminAuth import. Contains a fallback try/catch that re-queries without records_meta if the first query throws (handles the column not existing pre-migration-041). Its chain-alias normalization logic (CHAIN_STEP_MAP, ':' prefix stripping) is duplicated near-verbatim in src/app/api/admin/stats/route.ts — two independently maintained copies. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: FINDING (missing guard): no verifyAdminAuth — same presence-only-middleware exposure as history/runs/schedules. FINDING (silent swallow): TWO comment-only catch blocks that log nothing — :48 (the records_meta fallback, which also swallows a genuine DB failure and silently degrades every records_meta to null) and :107 (comment says 'pipeline_runs table may not exist yet', but it catches ANY error — a connection failure or timeout returns a 200 with an empty object, so the 'empty' and 'error' states are indistinguishable to the caller). They pass ESLint no-empty only because they contain a comment. FINDING (envelope): bare success object, string-valued error, unreachable wrapper. The migration-041 fallback at :49 is likely dead on a current DB (records_meta has long existed — it is selected unconditionally by the sibling /history route at :57) but I did not query the live schema to prove it. Census (pipeline_runs) CONFIRMED; no other table is touched. No SELECT *. | Caching: none observed — no dynamic/revalidate/Cache-Control (grep over src/app/api/admin/pipelines/ returned nothing). The header comment at :7-14 calls it a polling endpoint but no cache or TTL exists in code. | Locking tests: src/tests/chain.logic.test.ts, src/tests/quality.infra.test.ts.
